fatal_errors: The proposed carbon-fiber-reinforced Al-Li composite is unrelated to the target MgAlTiVFeCo high-entropy alloy.
The hypothesis omits the defining SPS treatment at 1000 °C and the required 800-1000 °C processing window.
It does not reconstruct the oxide barrier phases, densification, passive-film mechanism, or diffusion-controlled oxidation behavior.
No evidence supports the asserted improvements, particularly improved corrosion behavior, which cannot be assumed for a carbon-fiber/Al-Li galvanic couple.
explanation: The response addresses lightweight performance only at a very broad application level. It replaces the target ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo BCC alloy and SPS optimization with an entirely different Al-Li/carbon-fiber composite concept. Consequently, it misses the target processing conditions, dense oxide-bearing microstructure, passive-film and parabolic-oxidation mechanisms, quantitative density and hardness results, and electrochemical outcomes. Its proposed controlled comparison and measurements could test its own mechanical hypothesis, but the conditions are vague and no literature or experimental evidence is supplied. The corrosion claim is especially weak because carbon fibers can promote galvanic corrosion of aluminum alloys unless interfaces and exposure pathways are carefully controlled.
